signals.title: Ten motorcycles worth £40,000 stolen in four-minute raid on Welsh bike business
signals.summary: A gang of masked thieves has stolen ten brand-new off-road motorcycles from a storage facility in Wales, with the entire raid reportedly taking just four minutes. A motorcycle business in Carmarthenshire has been left counting the cost after a group of masked thieves broke into a storage facility and made off with ten new machines worth more than £40,000. The incident took place at around 4.20am on Thursday, October 29, at an overflow storage unit used by Absolute Motocross in Cross Hands, near Llanelli. According to the business's owner, Jordan Greville-Evans, the thieves appeared to know exactly where to go and which motorcycles were worth taking. The group is believed to have used a stolen white Ford Transit van to transport the motorcycles, arriving at the premises at approximately 4.19am before leaving just four minutes later. What makes the incident particularly concerning is the apparent level of preparation involved. The storage unit was located down a private lane and was being used temporarily while the business prepared to move into new premises. It wasn't the company's main dealership, and knowledge of its location was reportedly limited to staff and a small number of delivery drivers. Among the ten motorcycles taken were two 2024 Husqvarna TC250s, three 2026 Surron Ultra Bees, two 2025 Surron LBXs, two RFN SXE models and an RFN 70cc pit bike. Five of the motorcycles were already assembled, while the remaining five were still in their original crates. The thieves also appeared to have selected their targets carefully, leaving other motorcycles behind. Greville-Evans believes the group knew precisely what they were looking for, rather than simply taking whatever happened to be available. The stolen Transit van was subsequently discovered near the border and Liverpool, although there is reportedly an unexplained gap of around 40 minutes in its journey. This has raised questions about whether the motorcycles were transferred into another vehicle before the van was abandoned. The business has since launched an appeal for information, with its social media posts attracting millions of views. A £10,000 reward has also been offered for the safe return of all ten motorcycles. Dyfed-Powys Police confirmed that it is investigating a burglary at an address in Cross Hands during the early hours of October 29. The force said that damage was caused to the property and several off-road motorcycles were taken. The investigation remains ongoing. signals.title: BMW Motorrad invests in electric off-road startup with a very different attitude
signals.summary: Venna's Californian surf-and-motocross identity is a world away from BMW's traditionally buttoned-up approach, but the German manufacturer clearly sees something worth investing in. BMW Motorrad has invested in electric motorcycle startup Venna, a company whose laid-back Californian identity is about as far removed from Munich's traditionally straight-laced corporate culture as it gets. Venna specialises in high-performance electric motorcycles, with an initial focus on off-road riding. The investment will see the two companies combine their expertise in selected areas, with BMW bringing its experience in development, quality and industrialisation, while Venna retains its independence and ability to develop products at its own pace. There is, however, a slight catch. While Venna talks confidently about its electric motorcycle ambitions, it has yet to, as far as we can find, put a production bike into customers' hands. The company was previously known as Flux Performance, where it developed the Primo electric motocross prototype, a machine that attracted attention for its claimed performance and technology. Despite earlier production ambitions, the Primo never made it into customers' garages, and Venna has yet to announce a firm date for its first production model. That makes BMW's investment an interesting vote of confidence, as the German brand is effectively putting money behind a company with prototype development experience and plenty of ambition, but no proven track record of bringing a motorcycle to market. Turning an impressive electric dirt bike into a commercially viable product is a very different challenge, and it's one where BMW's manufacturing experience could prove invaluable. Whether Venna can turn its enthusiasm into something customers can actually buy remains the big question. Financial details of the deal, including the size of BMW's stake, have also not yet been disclosed. What's particularly interesting about the partnership is the contrast between the two brands. BMW Motorrad has built its reputation around precision engineering, technical development and a distinctly German approach to doing things. Venna, meanwhile, appears to have arrived from a rather different school of thought. In fact, most of the Venna webpage reads like it’s been penned by Point Break’s Bodhi. Sounding like a love letter to Southern California's surf, skate and motocross scenes, the Venna website talks about building a community around its motorcycles, hosting events at its Hollywood base and creating machines for riders who want to escape the everyday. The website's final line sums it up nicely: "We're building a bike and other rad s**t." Like, it’s cool and totally epic, maaan, but it's also hard to imagine that sentence making it into a BMW Motorrad internal strategy document. Behind the laid-back branding, however, is a serious engineering operation. Venna is the successor to Slovenian electric motorcycle developer Flux Performance, which attracted attention with its Primo electric motocross prototype. The company is led by Marko Ukota, who says BMW's investment will help accelerate the development of its technology and move towards industrial-scale production. BMW Motorrad CEO Markus Flasch says the partnership will help the company access new technologies and reach different groups of riders, particularly younger customers increasingly viewing motorcycles as recreational machines rather than everyday transport. Venna says it wants to develop high-performance electric motorcycles across multiple riding categories, although neither company has announced specific models or launch dates. For now, the pairing of Munich engineering and Californian motocross culture makes for an interesting combination. Whether BMW's influence will eventually tame Venna's more rebellious personality remains to be seen. signals.summary: Awalnya Coba-coba: Mulai Ganti Pelek, Sampai Jadi WR-V Gaya Racing JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Honda WR-V tidak hanya bisa tampil sebagai SUV ringkas untuk kebutuhan harian. Dengan sentuhan modifikasi yang tepat, mobil ini juga bisa memiliki tampilan lebih sporty dengan mengusung konsep racing look. Hal tersebut terlihat pada Honda WR-V milik Nurmi Agustin, atau yang akrab disapa Gusti. WR-V lansiran 2024. Merupakan mobil harian sekaligus kendaraan pertama yang dibeli atas nama sendiri. Gusti yang berdomisili di Tangerang membeli mobil tersebut pada November 2024. Seiring waktu, ketertarikannya terhadap dunia modifikasi mulai tumbuh setelah bergabung dengan komunitas pengguna WR-V. signals.title: Daftar Negara dengan Masa Berlaku SIM Terlama, Ada yang Seumur Hidup
signals.summary: Daftar Negara dengan Masa Berlaku SIM Terlama, Ada yang Seumur Hidup JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Setiap negara memiliki aturan berbeda terkait masa berlaku Surat Izin Mengemudi (SIM). Ada negara yang mewajibkan pengendara memperpanjang SIM setiap lima tahun, tetapi ada juga yang memberikan masa berlaku hingga puluhan tahun. Bahkan, ada negara yang menerapkan aturan SIM berlaku seumur hidup bagi warga negaranya. Kebijakan tersebut tentu berbeda dengan Indonesia yang menetapkan masa berlaku SIM selama lima tahun sejak tanggal penerbitan. Di sejumlah negara, masa berlaku SIM juga ditentukan berdasarkan usia pemiliknya. Selain itu, ada negara yang hanya mewajibkan pembaruan foto tanpa harus mengikuti ujian ulang. Dengan ketentuan tersebut, pemilik SIM tidak perlu melakukan perpanjangan secara berkala. Namun, aturan berbeda berlaku bagi warga negara asing. SIM Singapura yang dimiliki warga asing memiliki masa berlaku lima tahun sejak tanggal penerbitan. Namun, terdapat aturan yang memungkinkan masa berlaku SIM hingga pemiliknya berusia 65 tahun.
